text.p: European foreign and defence ministers met in Paris on Tuesday to debate ways of taking a greater role in the security affairs of their own continent.

The ministers from 28 countries, meeting under the auspices of the Western European Union (WEU), agreed to create a military committee within the WEU -- the EU's designated defence arm -- mirroring one in NATO which deals with military matters.
"The committee will facilitate the task of launching European-only operations," said one diplomat.
The meeting began with a wide-ranging discussion on the current situation in Albania where several European nations have sent a force to help re-establish peace in the chaotic Balkan country.
